title: Secure-context restriction
threats: network attacker or insecure transport reaches a powerful feature
secure_default: Expose powerful features only in secure contexts.
exception_questions: Is loopback or legacy compatibility exempted, and does the exception fail closed?
review_question: Is the feature restricted to a secure context at every exposure point?

title: Authenticated encrypted transport
threats: network observation, modification, credential theft, or downgrade
secure_default: Use authenticated encrypted transport by default.
exception_questions: Are cleartext local-network or constrained-device exceptions explicit and bounded?
review_question: Is authenticated encrypted transport the default, with cleartext exceptions explicit and fail-closed?

title: Origin or site boundary
threats: cross-origin data access or confused authority
secure_default: Keep data and authority origin-bound unless an explicit protocol grants access.
exception_questions: What cross-origin cases are allowed and what observable information remains?
review_question: Which data and operations cross an origin or site boundary, and what explicit gate applies?

title: CORS opt-in
threats: cross-origin response disclosure without server opt-in
secure_default: Require server opt-in before exposing a cross-origin response.
exception_questions: Are opaque, no-CORS, redirect, or credentialed cases bounded?
review_question: Does every cross-origin response exposure require an explicit server opt-in?

title: Permissions Policy gate
threats: untrusted embedded content invokes a powerful feature
secure_default: Use a restrictive default allowlist and explicit delegation.
exception_questions: Can nested frames or inherited policy broaden access?
review_question: What is the default allowlist and how is delegation constrained?

title: Permission and revocation lifecycle
threats: stale, ambient, or non-revocable authority
secure_default: Grant the minimum authority, expose revocation, and re-evaluate stale grants.
exception_questions: Are persistent or delegated grants exempt from fresh checks?
review_question: How are permission grant, denial, expiry, revocation, and delegation handled?

title: Fresh user activation or intent
threats: background, repeated, or attacker-induced high-impact action
secure_default: Require fresh user intent for high-impact actions.
exception_questions: If activation is optional, what normative visibility, frequency, or confirmation bound replaces it?
review_question: Which operations require fresh user intent and what common bound applies when activation is absent?

title: Content Security Policy integration
threats: script, style, navigation, or resource injection
secure_default: Compose with CSP and do not silently bypass applicable directives.
exception_questions: Which directives do not apply and why?
review_question: How does the feature compose with CSP, including redirects, inline content, and nested contexts?

title: Sandbox or isolated execution
threats: untrusted code or content reaches ambient authority
secure_default: Run untrusted content with the least ambient authority.
exception_questions: Which capabilities escape or relax the sandbox?
review_question: What code or content is untrusted and which sandbox boundary contains it?

title: Integrity or authenticity verification
threats: resource substitution, result corruption, or issuer impersonation
secure_default: Reject security-relevant input or results that lack verifiable integrity and provenance.
exception_questions: When is unsigned or unverifiable material accepted, cached, or displayed?
review_question: What independent evidence establishes integrity, authenticity, and acceptable provenance?

title: Input validation and rejection
threats: malformed or attacker-controlled input reaches sensitive processing
secure_default: Validate before use and reject invalid input without partial effects.
exception_questions: Are legacy, extension, or recovery paths more permissive?
review_question: What is validated, when does validation occur, and does failure prevent side effects?

title: Resource and complexity bounds
threats: CPU, memory, network, storage, or recursive-exhaustion denial of service
secure_default: Apply testable depth, size, time, rate, and memory bounds before expensive work.
exception_questions: Which bounds are implementation-defined, resettable, or bypassed by nested references?
review_question: Which resource limits apply recursively and how does exceeding one fail?

title: Fail-closed error behavior
threats: ambiguity, partial failure, or unavailable checks grant access
secure_default: Reject or stop safely when a required check is unavailable or ambiguous.
exception_questions: Can compatibility, recovery, cache, or offline paths continue after a failed check?
review_question: What happens when validation, permission, retrieval, or policy evaluation fails?

title: State or cache partitioning
threats: cross-site tracking, state inference, or cache-based XS-Leaks
secure_default: Partition state and caches by the narrowest applicable site or origin key.
exception_questions: Which shared, first-party-set, or compatibility cases bypass partitioning?
review_question: Which state is partitioned, by what key, and which observable exceptions remain?

title: Data minimization
threats: unnecessary collection, disclosure, retention, or secondary use
secure_default: Expose and retain only data necessary for the current purpose.
exception_questions: Are debugging, telemetry, fallback, or compatibility fields exempt?
review_question: Which fields or events are strictly necessary, and how are optional disclosures suppressed?

title: Precision reduction or privacy budget
threats: fingerprinting, timing inference, or cross-site state observation
secure_default: Minimize precision and frequency before exposing an observable signal.
exception_questions: Can multiple surfaces, origins, or repeated calls amplify the signal?
review_question: What precision, frequency, partition, and composition bounds apply to observable output?

title: Freshness and replay resistance
threats: reuse of stale authorization, credentials, assertions, or messages
secure_default: Bind security-relevant messages to freshness, context, and one-time state.
exception_questions: What clock, cache, retry, or offline exceptions accept stale material?
review_question: How are replay, expiry, retry, clock skew, and cached state handled?

title: Redirect and credential boundary
threats: credential forwarding, origin confusion, SSRF, or policy bypass through redirects
secure_default: Re-evaluate origin, credentials, and policy at every redirect.
exception_questions: Which redirects retain credentials or cross a trust boundary?
review_question: Are authorization, address, and policy checks repeated after every redirect?

title: External retrieval trust policy
threats: SSRF, substitution, cache poisoning, tracking, or unbounded dependency expansion
secure_default: Authenticate and bound external retrieval, redirects, address ranges, recursion, caching, and failure.
exception_questions: Can user-controlled URLs reach private networks, alternate schemes, or nested references?
review_question: What trust, address, integrity, redirect, cache, and resource policy applies to every nested retrieval?

title: Unspoofable trusted UI
threats: origin confusion, consent phishing, or misleading high-impact presentation
secure_default: Present origin, action, and consequence in user-agent-controlled UI.
exception_questions: Can minimal, fullscreen, installed, delegated, or background contexts hide the signal?
review_question: Which security-relevant facts are presented in unspoofable user-agent UI?

title: Canonicalization before comparison
threats: ambiguous identifiers, parser differentials, signature mismatch, or allowlist bypass
secure_default: Canonicalize with one specified algorithm before security-sensitive comparison.
exception_questions: Do display, signature, cache, and comparison paths use the same representation?
review_question: Which representation is canonical for parsing, comparison, signing, caching, and display?

title: Mixed-content blocking
threats: secure-context content incorporates attacker-modifiable subresources
secure_default: Block or safely upgrade insecure subresources without downgrade fallback.
exception_questions: Are local, optionally blockable, legacy, or redirect cases exempt?
review_question: Can any insecure resource enter a secure context through direct load, redirect, fallback, or cache?

title: Audit and accountability evidence
threats: undetected misuse, corruption, repudiation, or policy drift
secure_default: Produce bounded evidence that allows independent detection and disposition of misuse.
exception_questions: Who can suppress, modify, retain, or correlate audit data?
review_question: What evidence allows independent detection, rejection, investigation, and accountability?
